newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MIDF gets okay for stockbroking business.
newsitem.headline: MIDF gets okay for stockbroking business.

text.p: Malaysian Industrial Development Finance Bhd (MIDF) said it has received an in-principle approval from the finance ministry to start a stockbroking company in Kuala Lumpur.
The financial services firm said in a statement received on Tuesday it has formed MIDF Sisma Holdings Sdn Bhd and MIDF Sisma Securities Sdn Bhd to run the stockbroking business.

"MIDF Sisma Holdings Sdn Bhd and MIDF Sisma Securities Sdn Bhd were both given the approval in principle by the Committee of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange to be a corporate member of KLSE and a member company of the KLSE respectively," the statement said.
MIDF Sisma Holdings is 80 percent owned by MIDF and 20 percent by private company Sisma Vest Sdn Bhd. MIDF Sisma Securities is wholly-owned by MIDF Sisma Holdings.
MIDF Sisma Securities has an authorised capital of 100 million ringgit and will initially have the minimum-allowed paid-up capital of 20 million ringgit.
MIDF said it hoped to start operating the stockbroking arm before the end of this year.
MIDF owns a 78.4 percent interest in Oriental Bank Bhd and is also involved in finance, leasing, share registry and share issue services and in merchant banking.
